items.tier1_rationale: Brachial plexopathy is a broad descriptive term for any disease of the plexus, not a specific disease, and is not inherently vascular.
items.tier2_rationale: Brachial plexopathy is a diagnostic entity, but usually not primarily a vascular disorder.

items.parent_label: Inflammatory or Autoimmune Disorder with Neurological Involvement
items.tier1_rationale: IBD is an inflammatory/autoimmune disorder that can have neurological manifestations.
items.tier2_rationale: IBD is a disease family/umbrella, not a specific neuro entity under this parent.

items.parent_label: Inflammatory or Autoimmune Disorder with Neurological Involvement
items.tier2_rationale: Inflammatory brachial plexitis / neuralgic amyotrophy; synonym of inflammatory brachial plexus neuropathy.

items.parent_label: Traumatic or Compressive Disorder with Neurological Involvement
items.tier1_rationale: Brachial plexopathy is a broad term for any plexus dysfunction; while it fits the parent category of compressive disorders, it is not a specific disease.
items.tier2_rationale: Brachial plexopathy is a named entity commonly from trauma/compression.
Hypertension is specific but a systemic risk factor, not itself a vascular neuro leaf.

items.parent_label: Traumatic or Compressive Disorder with Neurological Involvement
items.tier1_rationale: Pancoast tumor causes compression of the brachial plexus.
items.tier2_rationale: Pancoast tumor is neoplastic; compressive effects do not make the disease traumatic/compressive.

items.tier1_rationale: Pancoast tumor can cause vascular compression (e.g., subclavian vein).
items.tier2_rationale: Pancoast tumor is neoplastic, not a primary vascular disorder.

items.parent_label: Inflammatory or Autoimmune Disorder with Neurological Involvement
items.tier2_rationale: Synonym of brachial plexitis (inflammatory brachial plexus neuropathy).
